content:
This week, a nonprofit code hosting platform in Berlin did something open source communities almost never do. It voted to turn work away.
Codeberg, the donation-funded, volunteer-run alternative to GitHub, passed a motion 358 to 144: no more projects that mostly consist of AI-generated code. A second motion passed alongside it, committing the platform to never train AI models on the code and data it hosts. About half the active membership showed up to vote. That’s a real decision by a real community, not a hot take from a founder’s blog.
The easy reading writes itself. FLOSS purists drawing a line against the machines. Craft versus slop. Flask creator Armin Ronacher, who now co-founds an AI agent company, called it “a very bad move” and asked the community to reconsider. Plenty of people on both sides are treating it as the latest skirmish in the culture war between people who love AI and people who hate it.
I think that reading is lazy. Read the actual announcement, the one titled Protecting our FLOSS commons from LLMs, and something else emerges.
It’s not a manifesto. It’s an invoice.
The Itemized Bill
